title: Expected rejected work
summary: A failing promise can be the correct result for invalid input. rejects tests that case explicitly.
introduction: A failing promise can be the correct result for invalid input. rejects tests that case explicitly. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A failing promise can be the correct result for invalid input. rejects tests that case explicitly.

blocks.code:
import { test, expect, vi, beforeEach, afterEach } from "vitest";
test("missing book", async () => { await expect(Promise.reject(new Error("No book"))).rejects.toThrow("No book"); });
blocks.title: Expected rejected work

blocks.text: The test passes when the promise rejects with the expected error.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Do not turn all errors into success just to make a test pass.
For more detail later, use this [Vitest further reading](https://vitest.dev/guide/).
